payoff: the a = c rule for no or infinitely many solutions
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. See why the no-solution rule works.

title: Perimeter 54, length 3 more than twice the width. Width?
hook: A rectangle's length is 2w + 3 and its perimeter is 54. Find w.
insight: Perimeter counts both lengths and both widths: 2(w + 2w + 3) = 54, so 6w + 6 = 54 and w = 8. Adding each side once gives the decoy w = 17.
visual: The rectangle's four sides peel off and line up end to end along a 54-unit ruler, two widths and two lengths, and w resolves to 8.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Count every side of the rectangle.

title: What does the 12 mean? Not the starting cost
hook: Kayak rental: C = 12h + 30. What does the 12 mean?
insight: 12 is the cost increase for each additional hour; 30 is the cost at h = 0, the flat fee. A 3-hour rental costs 30 + 36 = 66 dollars.
visual: A staircase climbs the line from (0, 30), each identical step labeled +12 per hour, while the first rung at 30 is labeled before any hours.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Expect "what does 12 represent?" on it.

title: Run over rise gives 1/3. The slope is 3
hook: A line passes through (2, 5) and (6, 17). What is its slope?
insight: Slope is change in y over change in x: (17 - 5)/(6 - 2) = 12/4 = 3. Then 5 = 3(2) + b gives b = -1, so y = 3x - 1.
visual: A right triangle grows under the segment, its vertical leg labeled 12 and horizontal leg 4, and the fraction 4/12 is struck in blue and flips to 12/4 = 3.
payoff: slope and equation from two points
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Rise over run, every single time.

title: $3.50 the first mile, $2.25 each additional: the m - 1 trap
hook: Taxi: $3.50 the first mile, $2.25 each additional mile. Cost for m miles?
insight: The first mile is already paid, so only m - 1 miles cost $2.25: C = 3.50 + 2.25(m - 1). The choice 3.50 + 2.25m charges the first mile twice: a 10-mile ride costs $23.75, not $26.
visual: A road of 10 mile-blocks: the first block is stamped $3.50, the other nine $2.25 each, and the (m - 1) in the equation brackets only the $2.25 blocks.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. "Each additional" means m - 1. Every time.

title: Up 6 every time x goes up 2. That's not a slope of 6
hook: f(0) = 1, and f rises 6 whenever x rises 2. What is f(10)?
insight: Convert to a per-1 rate first: 6/2 = 3, so f(10) = 1 + 3(10) = 31. Using 6 as the slope gives the trap 61.
visual: A staircase of wide steps, 2 across and 6 up, splits each step into two half-steps of 1 across and 3 up, and ten half-steps climb from 1 to 31.
payoff: rate-of-change questions from words and tables
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Turn every rate into per-one first.

title: This graph is f(x) + 4. So what is f(0)?
hook: y = f(x) + 4 crosses the y-axis at 10. What is f(0)?
insight: The graph shown is f lifted 4 units, so f itself is 4 lower: f(0) = 10 - 4 = 6. Reading 10, or adding to get 14, are the traps.
visual: The drawn line slides down 4 units onto a ghost copy labeled f, and its y-intercept dot drops from 10 to 6.
payoff: shifted-graph function questions in the hard module
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Check which graph you're actually looking at.

title: Slope of 3x - 5y = 10? -3/5 is the trap
hook: What is the slope of 3x - 5y = 10?
insight: B is -5, not 5, so -A/B = -3/(-5) = 3/5. Using B = 5 in -A/B gives the decoy -3/5.
visual: The rule -A/B takes in 3 and -5, the two minus signs meet and cancel in a small flash, and 3/5 is left in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. B carries its own sign. Keep it.

title: Perpendicular to slope 2/3 through (4, 1). Find the y-intercept
hook: Line through (4, 1), perpendicular to y = (2/3)x + 1. Its y-intercept?
insight: Flip and negate: the slope is -3/2. Then 1 = (-3/2)(4) + b = -6 + b, so b = 7. Only flipping (3/2) gives -5; only negating (-2/3) gives 11/3.

title: Pens $2, notebooks $5, total $40. Which equation?
hook: p pens at $2, n notebooks at $5, total $40. Which equation?
insight: Each price multiplies its own count: 2p + 5n = 40. The choice 5p + 2n = 40 pairs prices with the wrong items, and p + n = 40 counts items, not dollars.

title: Mix the subtraction order and you get 16. The answer is 8
hook: A line of slope 2 passes through (a, 4) and (10, a). Find a.
insight: Subtract in the same order top and bottom: (a - 4)/(10 - a) = 2, so a - 4 = 20 - 2a and a = 8. Writing (a - 4)/(a - 10) flips the sign and gives 16.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Infinitely many solutions: find b + c. Don't stop at b
hook: 2x+3y=9 and 6x+by=c: infinitely many solutions. Find b+c.
insight: Infinitely many means one equation is a multiple of the other: 6 is 3 times 2, so b = 9 and c = 27, and b + c = 36. Matching only the slope leaves c unknown.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Tickets: one equation counts, the other pays
hook: Adult $12, child $7. 50 tickets sold for $485. How many adults?
insight: One equation counts tickets, a + c = 50; the other counts dollars, 12a + 7c = 485. Substituting c = 50 - a gives 5a = 135, so 27 adults and 23 children.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: This point passes the first inequality. That's the trap

insight: (2, 4) satisfies y > 2x - 1 since 4 > 3, but fails y < -x + 5 since 4 is not less than 3. One failure kills a point; (1, 3) passes both.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: 2x - y >= 1 is shaded below the line. Here's why
hook: Graph 2x - y >= 1. Shade above or below the line?
insight: Solve for y first: -y >= 1 - 2x, and dividing by -1 flips it: y <= 2x - 1. So the region is below the solid line, even though the sign says greater.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: -3x + 7 > 19. Is it x > -4 or x < -4?
hook: -3x + 7 > 19. Is x greater than -4, or less?
insight: -3x > 12, and dividing by -3 mirrors the number line, so the sign flips: x < -4. Check x = -5: 15 + 7 = 22, which is greater than 19.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: At most 9 items, at least 150 g of protein. Most bars?
hook: Bars 10g, shakes 25g. At most 9 items, 150g protein minimum. Most bars?
insight: To maximize bars, give every other slot to shakes: 10b + 25(9 - b) >= 150, so 225 - 15b >= 150 and b <= 5. Five bars and four shakes give exactly 150 g; using only the 9-item limit gives the trap 9.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: Linear inequalities in 60 seconds
hook: Every SAT inequality question, from a number line to a shaded plane.
insight: Solve like an equation but flip for a negative; at least means >= and at most means <=; round whole-number answers by the story; a two-variable inequality keeps half the plane, dashed when strict; a system keeps the overlap.

title: 4^x + 4^x + 4^x + 4^x is not 16^x
hook: What is 4^x plus 4^x plus 4^x plus 4^x?
insight: Four copies of 4^x is 4 times 4^x, and one more factor of 4 adds one to the exponent. The sum is 4^(x+1), not 16^x or 4^(4x).

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: a^(3/2) = 64. The answer is not 96 or 512
hook: If a to the 3/2 power is 64, what is a?
insight: Undo the exponent by raising both sides to the 2/3 power: a = 64^(2/3) = (cube root of 64)^2 = 4^2 = 16. Check: 16^(3/2) = 4^3 = 64.

title: If 2^x = 5, what is 2^(x+3)? It's not 8
hook: 2^x = 5. What is 2^(x+3)?
insight: Adding 3 to the exponent multiplies by 2^3, so 2^(x+3) = 2^x times 8 = 5 times 8 = 40. A shift in the exponent is a hidden multiplier.
visual: The exponent x + 3 splits into two stacked factors, 2^x and 2^3, which become 5 and 8 and multiply to 40, while the guess 8 is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Exponent shifts are one of the SAT's favorite disguises.

title: If 3^x = 7, what is 9^x? Not 21
hook: If 3 to the x is 7, what is 9 to the x?
insight: 9 is 3 squared, so 9^x = (3^2)^x = (3^x)^2 = 7^2 = 49. Squaring the base squares the result; it does not triple it.
visual: The base 9 splits into 3 times 3, the expression regroups into (3^x)^2, and 7 drops in and squares to 49 while 21 is struck.
payoff: Rewriting a power with a new base
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. This base swap takes ten seconds once you see it.

title: (2/3)^-2 is not negative. Here's what it is
hook: What is two-thirds to the negative 2 power?
insight: A negative exponent means flip, not negative: (2/3)^-2 = (3/2)^2 = 9/4. The minus sign in an exponent never makes the answer negative.
visual: The fraction 2/3 rotates upside down into 3/2 as the minus sign fades from the exponent, then squares into 9/4, while -4/9 is struck in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Negative exponents flip. They never make things negative.

title: Why is 9^(1/2) the square root of 9?
hook: Why does a one-half exponent mean square root?
insight: Exponents add when you multiply, so 9^(1/2) times 9^(1/2) = 9^1 = 9. The number that times itself makes 9 is 3, the square root.
visual: Two equal strips labeled 9^(1/2) slide together into a 9-tile square, its side length reads 3, and the exponent label morphs into a root sign.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. One picture explains every fractional exponent you'll see.

title: What is half of 2^100? Not 2^50
hook: What is half of 2 to the 100th?
insight: 2^100 is 100 twos multiplied, and halving removes just one of them, so half is 2^99. 2^50 is the square root, an astronomically smaller number.
visual: A row of 100 small 2s loses a single 2 off the end to become 2^99, while the guess 2^50 shows half the row vanishing and gets struck.
payoff: Dividing powers of the same base
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Half of a power is not half the exponent.

title: Is 3 times 2^x the same as 6^x? Test x = 2
hook: Is 3 times 2 to the x the same as 6 to the x?
insight: No: at x = 2, 3 times 2^2 = 12 but 6^2 = 36. The 3 multiplies once while the base multiplies x times, so a coefficient can never merge into the base.
visual: At x = 2, one 3 sits beside two stacked 2s making 12 while two 6s make 36, and the two curves split apart on the grid.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Never merge the coefficient into the base.

title: Every SAT exponent rule in 60 seconds
hook: Every exponent rule on the SAT, in 60 seconds.
insight: Same base multiplied adds exponents, divided subtracts, a power of a power multiplies, x^0 = 1, a negative exponent flips, and a fraction exponent is a root over a power. Then rewrite everything with the same base.

title: Every SAT radical skill in 60 seconds
hook: Square roots on the SAT, everything you need, in 60 seconds.
insight: Pull out perfect squares, combine only like radicals, split roots over times but never over plus, treat a root as a 1/2 exponent, and rationalize by multiplying by 1. Then check radical equations for fake roots.

urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Every radical rule on one page, in one minute.

title: (ax + 3)(2x - 5) = 6x^2 + bx - 15. Find b
hook: (ax + 3)(2x - 5) = 6x^2 + bx - 15. What is b?
insight: The leading terms give 2a = 6, so a = 3. The middle term collects both cross products, 3x times -5 plus 3 times 2x = -9x, so b = -9, not -15 or 0.
visual: An area grid of 3x + 3 by 2x - 5 fills its four cells, the two cross cells light up in blue as -15x and +6x, and they merge into -9x.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. 'For all x' questions hinge on this middle term.

title: Why (x + y)^2 - (x - y)^2 is always 4xy
hook: Big square minus small square. Why is the leftover always 4xy?
insight: Four x-by-y rectangles arranged around a small square of side x - y form a big square of side x + y. Remove the small square and four rectangles, 4xy, remain.
visual: Four x-by-y tiles pinwheel around a small (x - y) square to build a large (x + y) square, the center square fades, and the four tiles glow in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. One pinwheel picture proves this identity.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: sqrt(25) is 5, but x^2 = 25 has two answers. Why?
hook: Is the square root of 25 equal to 5, or plus or minus 5?
insight: The root sign names one number, the nonnegative one, so sqrt(25) = 5. The equation x^2 = 25 asks for every number whose square is 25, so x = 5 or x = -5.
visual: The parabola y = x^2 is cut by the line y = 25 at x = -5 and x = 5, then the curve y = sqrt(x) draws only its upper branch and stops at a single 5.
payoff: Square roots versus solving x^2 = k
urgent_hook: {test} is today. One sign, one answer. One equation, two answers.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: x^2 + 8x = 9: complete the square on both sides
hook: Solve x squared plus 8x equals 9 by completing the square.
insight: Half of 8 is 4, so add 16 to both sides to get (x + 4)^2 = 25. Then x + 4 = 5 or -5, so x = 1 or x = -9; adding 16 to only one side is the trap.
visual: An x-square with two 4x strips folds into an L, a 4-by-4 corner fills in on both sides of the equals sign, and the full square reads (x + 4)^2 = 25.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Complete the square on both sides, every time.

title: y = c touches y = x^2 - 8x + 21 once. c is not 4

insight: A horizontal line touches a parabola once only at the vertex, which is at x = 4 with height 16 - 32 + 21 = 5. So c = 5; answering 4 gives the vertex's x, not its height.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: Sum of the solutions of 2x^2 - 12x + 7 = 0? Not 12

insight: The sum of the solutions is -b/a, and a is 2, so it is 12/2 = 6. Forgetting to divide by a gives the trap 12, and you never touch the irrational roots.

urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Sum of solutions in one line. Don't forget a.

title: Why the solutions of a quadratic add up to -b/a
hook: Why do the two solutions always add up to negative b over a?
insight: The roots sit the same distance d on either side of the axis x = -b/(2a), one at the axis plus d and one at the axis minus d. The ds cancel, so the sum is twice the axis: -b/a.

urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. The sum-of-roots shortcut, finally explained.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables

urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. A line can hit a parabola twice. Find both.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: |x + 4| = -2. How many solutions? Zero

urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. A distance can't be negative. Spot this in seconds.

insight: Squaring gives x^2 - x - 6 = 0, so x = 3 or -2. Check both: sqrt(9) = 3 works, but sqrt(4) = 2, not -2, so the only solution is 3.

urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Squaring creates fake answers. Check every root.

title: Tripling is a 200% increase, not 300%

title: V = 300(0.6)^t drops 40% a year, not 60%

insight: 0.6 is what remains each year, 60%, so the loss is 1 - 0.6 = 0.4, a 40% decrease. Answering 60% confuses what you keep with what you lose.

urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Keep versus lose: read decay bases correctly.

title: Grows 4% a year: is the base 1.4, 0.04 or 1.04?

insight: 4% is 0.04, and growth keeps the whole plus the extra, 1 + 0.04 = 1.04. The model is P = 2000(1.04)^t, while 2000(1.4)^t would be 40% growth.

urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Count the doublings, and the exponent writes itself.

insight: The square is smallest, zero, when x + 4 = 0, so x = -4 and the vertex is (-4, -7). Read the vertex's x as whatever makes the parentheses zero.

title: Maximum of f(x) = -2x^2 + 12x + 5? It's not 3

urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. The maximum is a height, not an x.

insight: The first three terms are a perfect square, x^2 - 2kx + k^2 = (x - k)^2, so f(x) = (x - k)^2 + 3. The minimum is 3, at x = k, whatever k is.

insight: Put -2 in parentheses everywhere x appears: (-2)^2 - 3(-2) = 4 + 6 = 10. Typing -2^2 squares only the 2, gives -4 and leads to the trap answer 2.

insight: Means only average evenly when the groups are the same size. Total points are 800 + 1,800 = 2,600 over 40 students, a mean of 65, pulled toward the bigger class.
visual: A seesaw holds 10 dots at 80 and 30 dots at 60, and the fulcrum slides from the struck 70 toward the heavier side, stopping at 65.
urgent_hook: Retaking {test}? Averaging averages is a hard-module trap. Fix it now.

skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
title: Remove 98 from 2, 3, 4, 5, 98. Which changes more?
hook: Remove 98 from 2, 3, 4, 5, 98. Which changes more, mean or median?
insight: The mean drops from 22.4 to 3.5 because the sum loses 98. The median only moves from 4 to 3.5, because it depends on the order of the values, not on how far away they are.
visual: Five dots sit on a line, the 98 dot slides off the page, the mean marker races left from 22.4 to 3.5, and the median marker shifts just half a step from 4.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. The outlier question is coming. Here's the 10-second answer.

title: This growth model says a 40-year-old is almost 11 feet tall
hook: Kids 2 to 10 grow about 2.5 inches a year. Predict height at 40.
insight: The model h = 2.5a + 31 only describes the ages it was fit on, 2 to 10. Plugging in 40 gives 131 inches, almost 11 feet, because the model doesn't know growth stops; its intercept, a height at age 0, lies outside the data too.
visual: A best-fit line runs through dots from ages 2 to 10, then extends as a dashed line far past the data while a little figure stretches to 131 inches and the dashed part is struck.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Know when a best-fit model stops making sense.

title: Given a student plays a sport, what's P(junior)? Not 30%
hook: 100 students, 40 athletes, 30 junior athletes. Given athlete, what's P(junior)?
insight: Given means you only look at athletes, so the denominator is 40, not 100: P = 30/40 = 0.75. Using 100 answers a different question, the chance of picking a junior athlete from everyone.
visual: A two-way table appears, everything outside the athlete column fades away, and the fraction 30/100 is struck as 30/40 = 0.75 forms in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Two-way tables are on every test. Get the denominator right.

skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
title: Why 1,000 people can describe 300 million
hook: How can 1,000 people tell you anything about 300 million?
insight: Like a spoonful from a well-stirred pot, a random sample reflects the whole no matter how big the pot is. Its precision depends on the sample size, not the population: 1,000 random people give a margin of about 3 percentage points.
visual: A small pot and a huge pot are stirred, the same spoonful is dipped from each, and both spoons show the same color mix while a plus-or-minus 3% readout stays fixed.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Understand why random samples work and inference gets easy.

title: A cube's surface area is 150. Most people botch the volume
hook: A cube has surface area 150. What is its volume?
insight: A cube has six equal faces, so one face is 150 / 6 = 25, the edge is 5, and the volume is 125. Taking the square root of 150 skips the six faces.
visual: The cube unfolds into a flat cross of six squares, the 150 splits into six chips of 25, and one face folds back up into a 5 by 5 by 5 cube.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Divide by six faces before anything else.

title: Why a box's surface area has a 2 in front
hook: Why is a box's surface area 2(lw + lh + wh)?
insight: A box has only three different faces, and each appears twice: front and back, top and bottom, left and right. A 3 by 4 by 5 box has 2(12 + 15 + 20) = 94.
visual: The box unfolds into its net and the six faces pair up, each matching pair sliding together in blue in turn, until three pairs sit side by side.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Three faces, each counted twice.

title: Diameter 6 is not radius 6
hook: A cylinder has diameter 6 and height 10. What is its volume?
insight: The radius is 3, so the volume is pi x 3^2 x 10 = 90pi. Plugging in 6 gives 360pi, four times too big.
visual: The 6 across the top is inked and struck, it halves into a radius of 3, and the cylinder fills as a stack of ten disks while the chip reads 90pi.
urgent_hook: {test} is in {days} days. Halve the diameter before you touch a formula.

title: The silo question: half a sphere, not a whole one
hook: A silo is a cylinder, radius 3, height 8, topped by a hemisphere. Volume?
insight: The cylinder is 72pi and the hemisphere is half of 4/3 pi x 27, which is 18pi, for 90pi. Adding the whole sphere, 36pi, is the trap.
visual: A full sphere drawn on top is struck, its lower half slides away into the cylinder's lid, and the readout adds 72pi + 18pi.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Read hemisphere as half, then add.

title: Double the radius, halve the height. Same volume?
hook: A cylinder's radius doubles and its height is cut in half. Volume?
insight: It doubles. The radius is squared, so doubling it multiplies the volume by 4, and halving the height divides by 2: 4 / 2 = 2.
visual: The cylinder widens and the volume chip jumps to x4, then it squashes to half height and the chip settles at x2 while the answer unchanged is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. The radius counts twice. Here is why.

title: Why the trapezoid formula averages the bases
hook: Why is a trapezoid's area the average of the bases times the height?
insight: Two copies of the trapezoid, one rotated, make a parallelogram with base b1 + b2 and the same height, and the trapezoid is half of it. Bases 4 and 10 with height 6 give 42.
visual: A copy of the trapezoid spins 180 degrees and slots in beside the original to form a parallelogram, then the blue copy fades back out leaving half.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Two trapezoids make a parallelogram.

title: Why two angles are enough for similar triangles
hook: Why do two matching angles make two triangles similar?
insight: Two angles force the third, since all three add to 180, so the shape is fixed and only the size can change. Every side then scales by one factor k.
visual: Two angle rays stay pinned at the ends of a base that stretches longer, and the triangle grows as an exact scaled copy while a k chip counts up.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Two angles fix the shape. Only size can change.

title: Tangent is just slope
hook: Why is tan 45 equal to 1?
insight: Tangent is opposite over adjacent, which is rise over run, so the tangent of an angle is the slope of a line at that angle. The line y = x rises 1 for every 1, so tan 45 = 1.
visual: A line rotates up from the x-axis with a rise-over-run triangle riding on it, and the tan readout matches the slope readout at every angle.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Tangent is slope. Watch them match.

title: tan A = 3/4 does not mean the sides are 3 and 4
hook: tan A = 3/4 and the hypotenuse is 30. What is the perimeter?
insight: The ratio fixes the shape, not the size: the sides are 3k, 4k and 5k. 5k = 30 gives k = 6, so the sides are 18, 24 and 30 and the perimeter is 72, not 12.
visual: A 3-4-5 triangle labeled with the ratio grows until its hypotenuse reaches 30, its legs ticking up to 18 and 24.
payoff: Find sides from a trig ratio
urgent_hook: Retaking on {date}? Ratio numbers are not side lengths. Scale them.

title: sin(2x + 10) = cos(3x - 20). Don't set them equal
hook: sin(2x + 10) = cos(3x - 20). What is x?
insight: A sine equals a cosine when the two angles add to 90: 5x - 10 = 90, so x = 20 and the angles are 50 and 40. Setting them equal gives x = 30 and two 70s, and sin 70 is not cos 70.
visual: The equation 2x + 10 = 3x - 20 is struck, then the two expressions slide into the acute corners of one right triangle and their sum chip reads 90.
urgent_hook: Scores out? Complementary-angle trig is a 750 question. Fix it before {test}.

title: Where 1, sqrt3, 2 comes from
hook: Why are the sides of a 30-60-90 triangle 1, sqrt3 and 2?
insight: It is half of an equilateral triangle with side 2: the base splits into 1 and 1, the hypotenuse is 2, and the height is sqrt(4 - 1) = sqrt3. A 45-45-90 is half a square, which is why its hypotenuse is s sqrt2.
visual: An equilateral triangle splits down its middle and one half swings away labeled 1, sqrt3, 2, then a square splits along its diagonal into two 45-45-90 halves.
payoff: Special right triangles on the reference sheet
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. The reference sheet triangles are just halves.

title: 30-60-90: which side gets the sqrt3?
hook: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the side opposite 60 is 9. Hypotenuse?
insight: The long leg is the short leg times sqrt3, so the short leg is 9/sqrt3 = 3sqrt3 and the hypotenuse is 6sqrt3, about 10.4. Doubling 9 to 18 treats the long leg as the short one.
visual: The reference sheet's triangle x, x sqrt3, 2x slides onto the problem, x sqrt3 matches the 9, and the answer 18 is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is in {days} days. Match x sqrt3 to the long leg first.

title: Arc length in radians is one multiplication
hook: Radius 4, central angle 2.5 radians. What is the arc length?
insight: 10: in radians, arc length is radius times angle, 4 x 2.5. Running 2.5 through the degree formula 2.5/360 x 8pi gives a tiny wrong answer.
visual: The degree formula is struck, then the radius wraps around the rim two and a half times, each wrap labeled 4, and the arc readout totals 10.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. In radians, arc length is r times theta.

title: Arc length is a fraction of the rim, not the area
hook: Radius 9, central angle 40 degrees. What is the arc length?
insight: 40 degrees is 1/9 of the circle, and the circumference is 18pi, so the arc is 2pi. Taking 1/9 of the area, 81pi, gives 9pi, which is the sector, not the arc.
visual: The rim unrolls into a straight 18pi segment and cuts into nine equal pieces, one glowing as 2pi, while the shaded sector reading 9pi is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Arc means rim. Sector means slice.

title: Diameter endpoints: the radius is half
hook: A diameter runs from (1, 2) to (7, 10). What is the circle's equation?
insight: The center is the midpoint (4, 6) and the diameter is 10 (a 6-8-10 triangle), so r = 5 and the equation is (x - 4)^2 + (y - 6)^2 = 25. Using 10 as the radius gives 100.
visual: The two endpoints pull toward their midpoint, a dashed 6-8-10 triangle measures the diameter, and it halves into a radius of 5 before the circle draws.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Midpoint for the center, half for the radius.

title: Completing the square: add to both sides
hook: x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y = 11. What is the radius?
insight: Complete both squares: (x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 = 11 + 9 + 16 = 36, so r = 6. Forgetting to add the 9 and 16 to the right side gives sqrt11.
visual: x^2 - 6x is drawn as a square with two strips and a 3 by 3 corner snaps in, the same happens for y with a 4 by 4, and both corner squares also drop onto the right side.
urgent_hook: Scores are out. Completing the square for circles is a 750 question. Fix it for {test}.

title: Inside or outside the circle? Compare squares
insight: Plug in: 4^2 + 4^2 = 32, and 32 is less than 36, so it is inside. Comparing 32 with the radius 6 says outside, which is wrong: compare squared distance with r^2.
visual: A dashed right triangle with legs 4 and 4 links the center to the point, the chip 32 sits beside 36, and the point dot sits just inside the rim.
payoff: Point inside, outside or on a circle
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Compare squares with squares.

title: Touching the x-axis means the radius is the y
hook: A circle centered at (-3, 5) touches the x-axis. What is its equation?
insight: The radius reaches straight down to the x-axis, so r = 5, the y-coordinate: (x + 3)^2 + (y - 5)^2 = 25. Using 3 makes it touch the y-axis instead.
visual: A circle grows from the center (-3, 5) until it kisses the x-axis, a vertical blue radius of 5 drops, and the r = 3 version touching the y-axis is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Tangent to the x-axis? The radius is the y.

title: Slide the corner around the circle. The angle never changes
hook: Slide this angle's corner around the circle. Why doesn't it change?
insight: An angle with its corner on the circle is half the central angle on the same arc. A central angle of 100 means every inscribed angle on that arc is 50, wherever the corner sits.
visual: A vertex slides around the rim while its two sides stay pinned to the arc's endpoints, and the angle readout stays locked at 50 beside a central 100.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Inscribed angles are half the central angle.

title: Every triangle in a semicircle is a right triangle
hook: Put a triangle's long side on a diameter. Why is the top always 90?
insight: Spin the triangle half a turn about the center: it and its copy form a quadrilateral whose diagonals are both diameters, equal and bisecting each other, which makes a rectangle. A rectangle's corners are 90.
visual: A triangle in a semicircle spins half a turn about the center, its copy completes a rectangle inside the circle, and the right-angle mark at the top lights up.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. A diameter always makes a right angle.

title: Every SAT circle question in 60 seconds
hook: Every SAT circle question uses one of five pictures.
insight: Arcs and sectors are fractions of the circle, radians measure angles in radius lengths, and the circle equation is Pythagoras with completing the square to find the center. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, and an inscribed angle is half the central one.
visual: One circle builds up idea by idea: a slice lifts out, a radius wraps the rim, a right triangle spins inside, a tangent touches, an inscribed angle slides along the edge, ending on a recap of slice, wrap, triangle, touch, half.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Every circle question in one minute.

title: Linear inequalities in 60 seconds: half planes and whole numbers
hook: y > 2x + 1. Where do all the answers live?
insight: Beats: a line splits the plane and the inequality keeps one side (dashed when strict), a system keeps only the overlap, a test point must satisfy every inequality, multiplying by a negative flips the sign, and a word problem's maximum count is the largest whole number that still fits.
visual: A dashed line draws and one side floods with accentWash, a second shaded region overlaps and only the lens stays, a test dot checks both, a number line mirrors at zero to turn 2 < 5 into -2 > -5, and a counter rounds 13.6 down to 13.
payoff: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Inequality questions are free points once you see the half plane.

title: Ratios, rates and units in 60 seconds
hook: Miles per hour, dollars per pound, feet per yard. One idea.
insight: Beats: a unit rate divides the thing by the per-thing; a conversion multiplies by a fraction equal to 1 so units cancel like variables; square units convert twice (1 yd^2 = 9 ft^2); a 2:3 part-to-part ratio means a whole of 5 parts; and a proportional relationship is a line through the origin.
visual: A chain of fractions cancels units like variables, a 1-yard square subdivides into 9 one-foot squares, a 2:3 bar splits into five equal blocks, then recipe points fall on a line through (0, 0).
payoff: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days out. Unit questions are fast points; here is the whole skill.

title: Two-variable data in 60 seconds: scatterplots and models
hook: A cloud of dots and one line. Four SAT questions hide here.
insight: Beats: a best-fit line predicts by reading the line, not a data point; its slope is the predicted change in y per one unit of x; its intercept is the predicted value at x = 0; a residual is actual minus predicted; and a bending cloud calls for the exponential or quadratic model.
visual: Scatter dots settle a line through themselves, a probe reads a prediction off the line, a slope triangle labels 'per 1 unit', residual sticks drop from dots to the line in accent, then the cloud bends and the line morphs into a curve.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Scatterplot questions read the line, never the dots.

title: SAT probability in 60 seconds: it's always which total
hook: One table, three probabilities, three different denominators.
insight: Beats: probability is favorable outcomes over all equally likely outcomes; a two-way table holds every count you need; 'given' throws away every row but one and makes that row's total the denominator; and working backward, a count is the probability times the total.
visual: A two-way table of 200 students lights its grand total, then 'given junior' fades every other row and the denominator morphs from 200 to 80, then a probability chip of 0.25 multiplies back into a count of 20.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Every probability question is choosing the right total.

title: Margin of error in 60 seconds: what a sample can claim
hook: The poll says 52%, plus or minus 3. Who is winning?
insight: Beats: a sample estimate comes with a range; 52% +/- 3 means anything from 49% to 55% is plausible, so the race is not settled; the range describes the population value, not individual people; a larger random sample usually shrinks the margin; and a population estimate is the sample proportion times the population size.
visual: Many sample bars scatter around a hidden true value, a bracket from 49 to 55 straddles the 50% line, then the sample-size counter grows and the bracket tightens while the scatter clusters.
payoff: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Margin-of-error questions all ask the same thing; see it once.

title: Every SAT Desmos move in 60 seconds
hook: The SAT gives you a graphing calculator. Five moves do most of the work.
insight: Beats: graph both sides and click the intersection to solve any equation; add a slider k and slide until two lines go parallel for 'no solution'; type y1 ~ m x1 + b to fit a table; graph two expressions to see whether they are one curve; and click a parabola to read its vertex and zeros.
visual: Drawn in our ink style, not a screen recording: two curves cross and a gray dot labels the intersection, a k slider tilts one line until parallel, table dots pull a regression line onto themselves, two formulas overlay into one curve, and a parabola's vertex dot lights.
payoff: every question type the built-in calculator can shortcut
urgent_hook: {test} is in {days} days. Practice these five Desmos moves before then.

title: Why 3 1/2 is a wrong answer on the SAT, even when it's right
hook: Your answer is three and a half. How do you type it?
insight: Not as a mixed number: typed without the space, 3 1/2 becomes 31/2, which is 15.5. The directions say to enter 7/2 or 3.5 instead.
visual: The characters 3, 1, /, 2 slide together in an entry box, the space collapses, a readout flips to 31/2 = 15.5 and is struck in blue, then 7/2 and 3.5 slide in beside it in accent.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Never type a mixed number into the answer box.

title: 'Of' means times, 'per' means divide: SAT words as math
hook: 'Of', 'per', 'is', 'less than'. Four words, four operations.
insight: 'Of' multiplies (30% of 60 = 0.3 x 60), 'per' divides (miles per hour = miles / hours), 'is' is the equals sign, and '5 less than x' is x - 5, written in the reverse order of the words.
visual: A word problem sentence sits on the page and each key word morphs in place into its symbol: 'of' into x, 'per' into a fraction bar, 'is' into =, and 'less than' swaps its two terms as it becomes a minus sign.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Translate every word problem with four words.

title: The slope formula works on curves too
hook: How fast does x^2 grow from x = 1 to x = 3?
insight: Average rate of change is slope between two points: (f(3) - f(1))/(3 - 1) = (9 - 1)/2 = 4. On a line every pair of points gives the same answer; on a curve it depends on the interval, which is how you tell them apart.
visual: A parabola draws, points at x = 1 and x = 3 join with a secant line whose slope triangle reads 8 over 2 = 4, then the points slide to other intervals and the readout changes, while on a line beside it the readout stays frozen.
payoff: average rate of change for linear, quadratic and exponential models
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. One formula for rate of change on any graph.

title: Solve for the box, not for x
hook: 3(2x+1) - 4 = 20. What is the value of 2x + 1?
insight: Treat 2x + 1 as one box: 3(box) - 4 = 20, so 3(box) = 24 and box = 8. Solving all the way gives x = 3.5, which is the trap choice.
visual: The group 2x + 1 shrinks into a single blue box, the equation reads 3(box) - 4 = 20, and the box fills with 8.
payoff: questions that ask for a grouped expression
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Watch for the box trick on it.

title: The two-second check that catches sign mistakes
hook: You got x = -2. Put it back in before you move on.
insight: Substitute into the original: 3 - 2(-2 - 4) = 3 + 12 = 15, so x = -2 checks. The decoy -10 gives 3 - 2(-14) = 31, not 15, so a sign error shows up instantly.
visual: The answer -2 drops into the x of the original equation and the left side computes in mono to 15 with a blue check, then -10 drops in, the readout lands on 31 and is struck.
payoff: any equation you can verify by substitution
urgent_hook: {test} is today. Plug each algebra answer back in before moving on.

title: The units tell you what any number in a model means
hook: C = 12h + 30. C in dollars, h in hours. Read the units.
insight: For 12h to be dollars, 12 must be dollars per hour, a rate. The 30 is added straight to dollars, so it is plain dollars: a one-time amount.
visual: Unit labels drop under each symbol, hours cancel against per hour like a fraction, and 12 is left wearing dollars per hour in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is on {date}. Read the units and the meaning reads itself.

title: Where the line hits the x-axis, the tank is empty
hook: W = 900 - 15d gallons after d days. When is the tank empty?
insight: Empty means W = 0: 15d = 900, so d = 60 days. The y-intercept, 900, is the starting amount; the x-intercept, 60, is when it runs out.
visual: The line slides down from (0, 900) as a drawn tank drains in step, and both reach zero together at d = 60.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Know what both intercepts mean.

title: The x-steps are uneven. Is this table still a line?
insight: Compare change in y to change in x, not y alone: 6/2, 3/1 and 9/3 are all 3, so it is the line y = 3x + 2.
visual: Slope triangles of different widths pop up between consecutive points, each labeled with its own ratio, and all three ratios collapse to the same 3.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Check ratios, not differences, on uneven tables.

title: The cover-up trick: both intercepts in three seconds
hook: 3x + 4y = 24. Find both intercepts without solving for y.
insight: Cover the y-term: 3x = 24, so the x-intercept is (8, 0). Cover the x-term: 4y = 24, so the y-intercept is (0, 6). Covering a term is setting that variable to 0.
visual: A card slides over 4y and 8 appears on the x-axis, then slides over 3x and 6 appears on the y-axis, and the line draws between them.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Learn the cover-up trick tonight.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Make the y's cancel with one multiplication
hook: 3x+2y=16 and 5x-4y=1. Multiply which one, by what?
insight: Double the first to get 6x + 4y = 32; now +4y and -4y cancel when you add: 11x = 33, so x = 3 and y = 3.5.
visual: A x2 stamp lands on the first equation, the +4y and -4y glow and collide to zero as the equations stack and add, leaving 11x = 33.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. One multiplication sets up every elimination.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Both equations start with y =? Set them equal
hook: y = x + 2 and y = 3x - 4. Solve it mentally.
insight: Both right sides equal y, so they equal each other: x + 2 = 3x - 4, so x = 3 and y = 5.
visual: The two y = fronts merge into one equals sign, the right sides face each other across it, and the lines' crossing point lights at (3, 5).
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Two y's? Set them equal and go.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Two numbers sum to 30 and differ by 8. Answer in three seconds
hook: x + y = 30 and x - y = 8. Find both, instantly.
insight: x is half of sum plus difference, (30 + 8)/2 = 19, and y is half of sum minus difference, (30 - 8)/2 = 11. Adding the equations is exactly this halving.
visual: Two bars of length 30 and 8 overlap, the extra 8 trims off, the remaining 22 splits into two 11s, and the 8 rejoins one of them to make 19.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. The halving trick solves these instantly.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Fractions in a no-solution system? Match one coefficient first
hook: (1/2)x + (3/4)y = 5 and kx + 3y = 2: no solution. k?
insight: Multiply the first by 4: 2x + 3y = 20. The y-terms now match, so the x-terms must match too: k = 2. Since 20 is not 2, the lines are parallel and there is no solution.
visual: A x4 stamp clears the fractions, the two 3y terms align in blue, and the k slot fills with 2 as the lines settle parallel.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Clear fractions, match one term, read k.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Can two lines share exactly two points? Never
hook: Can a system of two linear equations have exactly two solutions?
insight: Two points determine a line, so two lines sharing two points are the same line, with infinitely many solutions. That is why linear systems have only 0, 1 or infinitely many.
visual: Two lines cross at one dot; one line is grabbed and bent toward a second shared dot, and the moment it passes through both it snaps onto the other line entirely.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Zero, one or infinitely many. Never two.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Mixture problems are a seesaw
hook: Mix 10% and 30% to get 20 liters of 25%. How much each?
insight: 25 is 15 away from 10 but only 5 away from 30, so the amounts balance 1 to 3, with more of the closer one: 5 liters of 10% and 15 liters of 30%.
visual: A seesaw lies on a number line from 10 to 30, the pivot slides to 25, and weights of 5 and 15 liters drop on opposite ends until it balances.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Try the seesaw on any mixture.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: $40 + $15 a month vs $70 + $10 a month. When do they tie?
hook: Plan A: $40 plus $15 a month. Plan B: $70 plus $10. When equal?
insight: B starts $30 higher but gains on A by $5 every month, so the gap closes in 30/5 = 6 months, when both cost $130. After that, B is cheaper.
visual: Two lines start 30 apart on the y-axis, a vertical gap bar between them shrinks by 5 at each month tick, and it vanishes at month 6 where a blue dot marks $130.
payoff: break-even and "when are they equal" questions
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Gap divided by closing speed is the meeting point.

title: The 10-second way to check 'which is equivalent'
hook: Which expression is equivalent? Don't expand. Plug in x = 2.
insight: Equivalent expressions match for every x, so pick an easy value like x = 2, evaluate the question and each choice, and keep the match. Avoid 0 and 1, which make several choices tie.
visual: The value 2 drops into the question and four answer choices like a probe, each prints a number in mono, and only the matching choice stays ink while the rest fade.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Check any equivalent-expression answer by plugging in 2.

title: Expanding (3x - 4)(2x + 5)? Compute only the term that differs
hook: Which is equivalent to (3x - 4)(2x + 5)? Look at the choices first.
insight: If every choice starts with 6x^2 and ends with -20, only the middle term decides it: 3x times 5 plus -4 times 2x = 15x - 8x = 7x. The answer is 6x^2 + 7x - 20.
visual: Four answer choices stack up, their matching first and last terms fade to gray, and only the middle terms stay ink as the cross products 15x and -8x combine into 7x.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Read the choices before you expand anything.

title: Which is a factor of 2x^2 + 5x - 3? Test the zeros
hook: Which is a factor of 2x squared plus 5x minus 3?
insight: A factor (2x - 1) means x = 1/2 makes the polynomial zero, and 2(1/4) + 5/2 - 3 = 0, so 2x^2 + 5x - 3 = (2x - 1)(x + 3). Test each choice's zero instead of factoring.
visual: Each answer choice drops its zero onto the x-axis under the parabola, three miss the curve, and 1/2 lands exactly on a crossing in blue.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Find the factor without factoring anything.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: Solve x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0 without the full formula
hook: Solve x squared minus 6x plus 4 equals 0 in one line.
insight: For x^2 + bx + c, the roots sit at the midpoint -b/2, plus or minus sqrt((b/2)^2 - c). Here the midpoint is 3 and the distance is sqrt(9 - 4), so x = 3 plus or minus sqrt(5).
visual: A dot lands on the parabola's axis at x = 3, then two equal arrows of length sqrt(5) reach out left and right to the crossings.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Midpoint plus or minus a distance. That's the formula.

title: Grow each side of a square by 10%. Its area grows by 21%
hook: Each side of a square grows 10%. How much does its area grow?
insight: Area multiplies the two sides, so the factor is 1.1 x 1.1 = 1.21: a 21% increase, not 20%. The extra 1% is the small corner square where the two new strips meet.
visual: A 10-by-10 square grows a blue 1-unit strip on the right and on top, and the tiny 1-by-1 corner where the strips meet glows as the readout climbs from 20% to 21%.
payoff: percent change of a product, scale and area
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Percent questions about area hide this extra 1%.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: How many 1 cm cubes fill a 1 meter box? A million
hook: How many 1-centimeter cubes fit inside a 1-meter cube?
insight: Each edge holds 100 little cubes, and volume multiplies three edges: 100 x 100 x 100 = 1,000,000. A liter is a 10 cm cube, 1,000 cubic centimeters, so a cubic meter is 1,000 liters.
visual: A row of 100 tiny cubes extrudes into a 100-by-100 sheet, the sheet stacks into a full meter cube, and the counter jumps 100, 10,000, 1,000,000.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Cubic units hide a factor most people forget. Cube it.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: The unit mix-up that lost a NASA spacecraft
hook: In 1999, NASA lost a Mars orbiter over one missing unit conversion.
insight: One team's software reported thruster impulse in pound-force seconds, and the navigation software read it as newton-seconds. A pound-force is about 4.45 newtons, so the trajectory was wrong and the Mars Climate Orbiter was lost.
visual: Two number chips labeled pound-force seconds and newton-seconds slide into one equation without a conversion, the planned orbit arc dips inside the planet's atmosphere line, and the missing x 4.45 appears in blue.
payoff: why units must cancel in every conversion
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Write the units on every number. Here's why.

skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
title: Weights at 1, 2, 3 and 10 on a ruler. Where does it balance?
hook: Weights at 1, 2, 3 and 10 on a ruler. Where does it balance?
insight: At the mean, 4. The weights at 1, 2 and 3 sit 3, 2 and 1 below it, a total of 6, and the weight at 10 sits exactly 6 above: the mean is the point where distances below and above cancel.
visual: Four weights rest on a ruler over a sliding fulcrum; distance arms from each weight to 4 appear, the three left arms join into one length of 6 that matches the right arm, and the ruler levels.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Picture the mean as a balance and data questions get easy.

title: A 99% accurate test says you're sick. The chance you are: 9%
hook: Disease: 1 in 1,000. Test: 99% accurate. You test positive. Chance you're sick?
insight: Picture 100,000 people: 100 are sick and 99 of them test positive, but 1% of the 99,900 healthy people, 999, also test positive. Given positive, P(sick) = 99/1,098, about 9%.
visual: A crowd of 100,000 dots splits into a tiny sick cluster and a huge healthy field, the positives light up blue in both, and the small sick share of the blue dots shrinks the answer to 9%.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. This puzzle changes how you read 'given' forever.

title: Never measure a weird shape. Subtract it
hook: A circle fits snugly inside a 10 by 10 square. Shaded corners' area?
insight: Whole minus hole: the circle's diameter is 10, so its radius is 5 and the corners are 100 - 25pi, about 21.5.
visual: The circle lifts out of the square like a cookie cutter, leaving four curved corner pieces whose chip reads 100 - 25pi.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Every shaded region is whole minus hole.

title: Every SAT volume formula is one rule
hook: Box, cylinder, cone, pyramid. One rule covers all four formulas.
insight: Straight solids are base area x height, lwh and pi r^2 h, and pointed solids are one third of that. Only the sphere breaks the pattern, and it is on the reference sheet.
visual: The reference sheet's volume row lights up, then each base extrudes upward into its prism while the pointed twin beside it shrinks to one third.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Four volume formulas, one rule.

title: A square's area is half its diagonal squared
hook: A square has a diagonal of 10. What is its area?
insight: 50, with no side length needed. Tilt the square 45 degrees inside a 10 by 10 box: the four corner triangles fold in and cover it exactly, so its area is d^2 / 2.
visual: The four corner triangles of the box fold inward like envelope flaps and cover the tilted square exactly, the area chip halving 100 to 50.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Diagonal squared, halved. That is the square's area.

title: The exterior angle shortcut
hook: Exterior angle 130. One far interior angle is 50. The other?
insight: 80. The exterior angle equals the sum of the two far interior angles, so 130 - 50 = 80, with no need to find the third angle first.
visual: The two far corners of the triangle slide over and fit exactly inside the exterior angle, 50 and 80 stacking to 130.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. One subtraction solves exterior angles.

title: Parallel lines hand you similar triangles for free
hook: Bowtie: AC is 6, CE is 9, AB is 4. Find DE.
insight: With AB parallel to DE, the vertical angles at C and the alternate angles make the triangles similar with ratio 9/6 = 1.5, so DE = 6. Match A with E and B with D, not by position on the page.
visual: Triangle ABC spins half a turn about C and stretches by 1.5 until it lands exactly on triangle EDC, each vertex label sliding onto its partner.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. A bowtie between parallel lines is always similar.

title: Spot the triple, skip the square roots
hook: Legs 16 and 30. What is the hypotenuse?
insight: 16 and 30 are 2 x 8 and 2 x 15, so this is an 8-15-17 triangle doubled: 34. Know 3-4-5, 5-12-13 and 8-15-17 and their multiples.
visual: A small 8-15-17 triangle doubles in size onto the given one, and its hypotenuse label 17 becomes 34.
urgent_hook: {test} is in {days} days. Three triangles save you every square root.

title: The ladder slides 4 feet down. How far does the base move?
hook: A 25-foot ladder's base is 7 feet out. The top slides down 4. Base?
insight: The top starts 24 feet up (7-24-25) and drops to 20, so the base moves to 15 (15-20-25). It slides 8 feet, not 4.
visual: The ladder slides down the wall with dashed right triangles traced at the start and the end, and the base readout moves from 7 to 15.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Guess how far the base slides.

title: Backsolve: let the SAT's answer choices do the algebra
hook: The square of a positive number is 12 more than the number. Which?
insight: With choices 3, 4, 6 and 12, plug in instead of solving: 3 gives 9 vs 15, too small, and 4 gives 16 = 16, done. Any multiple-choice question with numeric choices can be checked this way, and the direction of a miss tells you which way to move.
visual: Four answer cards sit in a row; the 3 card drops into x^2 = x + 12 and a balance tips short, the 4 card drops in and the balance levels in accent, and the remaining cards fade.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. When the algebra stalls, the choices can finish it.

title: 35 minutes, 22 questions: the SAT math clock in one picture
hook: 35 minutes for 22 questions. How long do you really get?
insight: About 95 seconds each on average, but each module runs from easiest to hardest, so the early questions should take far less and bank time for the last few, where the hard ones sit.
visual: A 35-minute clock face splits into 22 equal wedges of about 95 seconds, then the early wedges shrink and the late wedges widen as a ramp of question difficulty draws beneath it.
urgent_hook: {test} is in {days} days. Here is how to spend your 35 minutes.

title: SAT figures are drawn to scale unless they say otherwise
hook: Is this angle 40 degrees or 70? Just look at it.
insight: The math directions say figures are drawn to scale unless a note says otherwise, so the picture is evidence: an angle that looks acute is acute, and a segment that looks twice as long is close to it. Use it to throw out impossible choices before you compute.
visual: A triangle figure sits beside four answer choices; a protractor overlay swings onto the angle and reads about 40, and the choices 70 and 110 are struck in blue before any algebra begins.
urgent_hook: {test} is in {days} days. The figures are drawn to scale; use them.

title: Stuck on 'which expression is equivalent'? Plug in x = 2
hook: Which is equivalent to (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3)? Try x = 2.
insight: At x = 2 the expression is (4 - 9)/(2 - 3) = 5, and of the choices x + 3, x - 3, x^2 - 3 and x + 9, only x + 3 also gives 5. Equivalent expressions agree at every x, so one test value rules out the rest; avoid 0 and 1, which make too many choices tie.
visual: The expression and four choices sit in a column; x = 2 drops into each like a probe, readouts show 5, -1, 1 and 11, and three choices are struck in blue while x + 3 stays in accent.
payoff: equivalent expressions and variable answer choices
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. One test number cracks every 'equivalent' question.

title: What to fix before your SAT retake: frequency times misses
hook: Scores are in. What do you fix first for the retake?
insight: Rank each missed pattern by how often it appears times how often you miss it: a slope-interpretation miss that shows up several times a test outranks one rare circle question. Fix the top three first; most will sit in Algebra and Advanced Math, about 70% of the section.
visual: Your misses drop as dots onto a grid with 'how often on the test' across and 'how often you miss it' up, the top-right corner shades in accentWash, and three dots in it light up as the plan.
urgent_hook: Retaking on {date}? Fix these patterns first, in this order.

title: The $75 fee is charged once, not every hour
hook: $75 to show up, $40 an hour, bill $235. How many hours?
insight: The fee happens once, so it is the constant: 75 + 40h = 235, 40h = 160, h = 4. Putting the fee on the rate term, 75h + 40 = 235, gives the decoy 2.6.
visual: A bill builds as one wide $75 block, then $40 blocks snap on one per hour until the total reads 235 after the fourth block.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Fixed fee once, rate every time.

title: 2x + ky = 7 is parallel to y = -4x + 1. k isn't -4
hook: 2x+ky=7 is parallel to y = -4x + 1. What is k?
insight: Parallel means equal slopes: the first slope is -2/k, so -2/k = -4 and k = 1/2. Copying -4 into k is the trap.
visual: The line 2x + ky = 7 pivots as k slides and locks parallel beside y = -4x + 1 exactly when the chip reads k = 0.5.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Parallel means equal slopes, nothing else.

title: 8 is eggs per tray. What is 8t?
hook: Eggs: 12c + 8t = 480 for cakes and trays. What is 8t?
insight: 8 is eggs per tray, but 8t is the total eggs used for all t trays. 480 is all the eggs, and 12c is the eggs for all the cakes.
visual: A single tray of 8 eggs copies itself t times into a row, the row brackets as 8t, and it joins the cakes' 12c bracket to fill a 480 bar.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Coefficient or whole term? Read it twice.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
title: Same y-intercept, so no solution? It has exactly one
hook: y = 2x + 1 and y = -2x + 1. How many solutions?
insight: The number of solutions depends on the slopes first: different slopes always cross exactly once, here at (0, 1). Intercepts only matter when the slopes are equal.
visual: Both lines draw from the same point on the y-axis, the words no solution are struck in blue, and a dot marks their single crossing at (0, 1).
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Different slopes mean exactly one solution.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: "No more than $60": which way does the sign point?
hook: $15 entry, $9 per game, spend no more than $60. Which inequality?
insight: "No more than" is a ceiling, so the total is <= 60: 15 + 9g <= 60. "At least" and "no fewer than" are floors, written >=. Say "this or less" out loud to check.
visual: The words no more than morph into a ceiling line at 60 on a number line, the total slides up and stops beneath it, and a reversed >= is struck in blue.
payoff: translating at least and at most
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Ceiling or floor? Read the phrase twice.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
title: The point is on the line. It's still not a solution
hook: Is (2, 3) a solution of y > x+1? It's on the line.
insight: On the line, y = x + 1 exactly: 3 = 3. A strict > excludes equality, which is why the boundary is dashed, so (2, 3) is not a solution. With >= the line is solid and it would be.
visual: A dashed boundary line, a dot at (2, 3) resting right on it, the check 3 > 3 inks false, and the dot fades as the dashes pulse.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Dashed means the line itself doesn't count.

title: (16x^8)^(1/4): the 16 gets rooted too
hook: What is 16 x to the eighth, all to the one-fourth power?
insight: The outside exponent hits every factor: 16^(1/4) = 2 and (x^8)^(1/4) = x^2, so the answer is 2x^2. Leaving the 16 alone gives the trap 16x^2.
visual: The exponent 1/4 sends two arrows inside, one shrinking 16 to 2 and one shrinking x^8 to x^2, and 16x^2 is struck in blue.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. The outside exponent hits everything inside. Every time.

title: What is 2^2024 - 2^2023? Not 2
hook: What is 2 to the 2024 minus 2 to the 2023?
insight: Factor out the smaller power: 2^2023(2 - 1) = 2^2023. Subtracting exponents only works for division, never for subtraction.
visual: 2^2024 splits into 2 times 2^2023, the shared 2^2023 slides out front, 2 - 1 collapses to 1, and the guess 2^1 is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Factor out the smaller power and watch it collapse.

title: x^3 times x^4 is not x^12
hook: What is x^3 times x^4?
insight: Write it out: three x's times four x's is seven x's in a row, so x^3 times x^4 = x^7. Exponents multiply only for a power of a power, like (x^3)^4 = x^12.
visual: Three x tiles and four x tiles slide together into one row of seven, while a 3-by-4 grid of twelve tiles appears beside it and is struck in blue.
payoff: Multiplying powers with the same base
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Add exponents or multiply them? Get it right every time.

title: 2x^(-2) is not 1/(2x^2). The 2 stays put
hook: Which is equivalent to 2x to the negative 2?
insight: The exponent belongs only to x, so only x moves: 2x^(-2) = 2/x^2. Moving the 2 down as well gives 1/(2x^2), which is off by a factor of 4.
visual: The negative exponent sends x down below a fraction bar while the coefficient 2 stays upstairs, and the trap 1/(2x^2) is struck in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. A negative exponent moves only its own base.

title: 1/x + 1/(x + 1) is not 2/(2x + 1)
hook: What is 1 over x plus 1 over x plus 1?
insight: Never add denominators; use the common denominator x(x + 1) to get (2x + 1)/(x(x + 1)). Test x = 1: 1 + 1/2 = 3/2 matches, while 2/3 does not.
visual: Two fraction bars try to merge tops and bottoms and get struck in blue, then each fraction stretches to the shared denominator x(x + 1) and the numerators add.
urgent_hook: {test} is today. One calm reminder: never add the denominators.

title: (x^2 + 9)/(x + 3) does not simplify to x + 3
hook: Does x squared plus 9, over x plus 3, simplify to x plus 3?
insight: No: only a difference of squares factors, x^2 - 9 = (x + 3)(x - 3), while x^2 + 9 has no real factors. Test x = 1: 10/4 = 2.5, not 4.
visual: x^2 - 9 splits cleanly into two factors, x^2 + 9 tries the same split and fails, and the test value x = 1 prints 2.5 against 4 with x + 3 struck.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. A plus sign changes everything here.

title: Why plugging in -2 gives the remainder instantly
hook: Divide x squared plus 5x plus 9 by x plus 2. What's left over?
insight: Any division can be written p(x) = (x + 2)q(x) + r, and at x = -2 the (x + 2) part vanishes. So r = p(-2) = 4 - 10 + 9 = 3, and x^2 + 5x + 9 = (x + 2)(x + 3) + 3.
visual: The identity (x + 2)q(x) + r sits on the page, x = -2 drops in, the product term fades to zero in gray, and the remainder 3 stays in blue.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Find a remainder without long division.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: 1/R = 1/a + 1/b. Why R is not a + b
hook: 1/R = 1/a + 1/b. Solve for R.
insight: Combine first, then flip: 1/R = (a + b)/(ab), so R = ab/(a + b). Flipping term by term to get a + b fails: with a = b = 2, R is 1, not 4.
visual: Two fractions merge over the common denominator ab, the single fraction flips upside down in one motion, and a + b is struck using the test values a = b = 2.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. You can't flip a sum term by term.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: Multiply the roots of 2x^2 - 7x - 15 = 0 without solving
hook: 2x^2 - 7x - 15 = 0. What is the product of its solutions?
insight: The product of the solutions is c/a = -15/2. Check: the equation factors as (2x + 3)(x - 5), with solutions -3/2 and 5, whose product is -15/2.
visual: A rectangle with sides -3/2 and 5 forms from the two roots, its signed area reads -15/2, and the formula c/a lights up with the a = 2 underlined in blue.
urgent_hook: Retaking on {date}? Learn c/a now. {days} days is plenty.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: sqrt(2x + 3) + 3 = 0. Squaring says x = 3. Wrong
hook: Solve the square root of 2x plus 3, plus 3, equals 0.
insight: Isolate the root first: sqrt(2x + 3) = -3, and a square root is never negative, so there is no solution. Squaring blindly gives 2x + 3 = 9 and the fake x = 3.
visual: The root term isolates on the left, its graph sits entirely above the axis, and the line y = -3 runs below it untouched while x = 3 is struck.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Isolate the root, then look at the sign.

skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
title: 3x^2 - 18x - 15 = 0. Find x^2 - 6x without solving
insight: Divide every term by 3: x^2 - 6x - 5 = 0, so x^2 - 6x = 5. The quadratic formula works too, but it takes a minute and invites errors.
visual: Every coefficient divides by 3 in one sweep, the target x^2 - 6x lights up in blue inside the new equation, and the -5 slides across to become 5.
payoff: Structure questions that ask for an expression
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Look for the asked expression before you solve.

title: 500(1.2)^t in years. Rewrite it in months
hook: f(t) = 500(1.2)^t with t in years. Rewrite with m in months.
insight: m months is m/12 years, so substitute t = m/12 to get 500(1.2)^(m/12). The trap 500(1.2)^(12m) would grow 20% twelve times every month.
visual: A year timeline stretches into 12 month ticks, t morphs into m/12 inside the exponent, and at m = 12 the exponent readout shows exactly 1.
payoff: Changing time units in exponential models
urgent_hook: Retaking on {date}? Hard-module exponentials love unit changes. Fix this first.

title: 9^(x/2) is not 4.5^x
hook: Which is equivalent to 9 to the x over 2?
insight: Halving the exponent square-roots the base: 9^(x/2) = (9^(1/2))^x = 3^x. Dividing the base by 2 to get 4.5^x is the trap.
visual: The exponent x/2 splits into 1/2 and x, the 1/2 slides down onto the 9 and shrinks it to 3, and the curves of 3^x and 9^(x/2) land on top of each other.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Halve the exponent, root the base.

title: Which form shows the minimum of this parabola for free?
hook: (x-1)(x-5) or (x-3)^2 - 4: which shows the minimum?
insight: (x - 1)(x - 5), (x - 3)^2 - 4 and x^2 - 6x + 5 are equal, but only vertex form displays the minimum, -4 at x = 3. Factored form shows the zeros 1 and 5, and standard form the y-intercept 5.
visual: The three expressions sit in a row, a minimum readout probes each one, and only the vertex form lights -4 directly while the factored form is struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Pick the form that shows the answer.

title: h = -16t^2 + 64t + 80. When does it land? Not t = -1
hook: h = -16t^2 + 64t + 80. When does the ball hit the ground?
insight: Landing means h = 0: -16(t^2 - 4t - 5) = -16(t - 5)(t + 1) = 0. Time can't be negative, so the ball lands at t = 5 seconds.
visual: The ball's arc draws over a time axis, the curve's left crossing at t = -1 is struck as before launch, and the landing at t = 5 lights up in blue.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Context rules out one root. Know which.

title: f(-4) = 0. Is the factor (x - 4) or (x + 4)?
hook: The table shows f of negative 4 equals 0. Which must be a factor?
insight: A zero at x = -4 means the factor equals 0 when x = -4, and that is x + 4, not x - 4. The factor's sign is always the opposite of the zero's.
visual: The table row with output 0 lights up, x = -4 drops into both candidate factors, and only x + 4 turns to 0 while x - 4 reads -8 and is struck.
payoff: Zeros and factors from tables and graphs
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. A zero at -4 means a factor of x + 4.

title: In h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 20t + 1.5, what does 1.5 mean?
hook: h of t equals negative 4.9t squared plus 20t plus 1.5. What's 1.5?
insight: Plug in t = 0: every t term vanishes and h(0) = 1.5. It is the height at launch, not the maximum height or a speed.
visual: The time slider rewinds to t = 0, the -4.9t^2 and 20t terms fade to gray, and the arc's starting point lights up at 1.5 on the height axis.
payoff: Initial value of a nonlinear function
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. The constant term is where the story starts.

title: f's vertex is (2, 5). Where is the vertex of f(x - 3) + 2?
hook: f's vertex is (2, 5). Vertex of f(x - 3) + 2?
insight: Inside the parentheses, x - 3 moves the graph 3 to the right; outside, + 2 moves it up 2. The new vertex is (5, 7), not (-1, 7).
visual: The parabola glides right 3 as an inside dial turns, then up 2 as an outside dial turns, and the vertex readout updates to (5, 7) in blue.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Inside moves sideways, opposite the sign. Outside moves up.

title: (3, 4) is on f. Which point is on f(-x)?
hook: (3, 4) is on f. Which point is on y = f(-x)?
insight: f(-x) needs an input of -3 to feed 3 into f, so the point is (-3, 4), a flip across the y-axis. -f(x) flips outputs instead, giving (3, -4).
visual: The curve mirrors left to right across the y-axis carrying (3, 4) to (-3, 4), then a ghost copy flips up and down to (3, -4) to show the other reflection.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. f(-x) and -f(x) are different flips.

title: f(2x) squeezes the graph. Where does (6, 1) go?
hook: The point 6, 1 is on f. Which point is on f of 2x?
insight: f(2x) needs 2x = 6 to reach the same output, so x = 3 and the point is (3, 1). Changes inside act opposite, so multiplying by 2 squeezes the graph to half its width.
visual: The graph squeezes horizontally toward the y-axis like an accordion, carrying (6, 1) to (3, 1), while (12, 1) is struck in blue.
urgent_hook: Retaking on {date}? Inside changes act opposite, even for multiplying.

title: f(x) = x^2 + 2x. What is f(x + 1)?
hook: f(x) = x^2 + 2x. What is f(x + 1)?
insight: Replace every x with (x + 1): (x + 1)^2 + 2(x + 1) = x^2 + 4x + 3. Writing x^2 + 2x + 1 adds 1 to the output instead of the input.
visual: Each x in the formula swells into a box labeled (x + 1), the boxes expand into tiles, and like terms collect into x^2 + 4x + 3 while x^2 + 2x + 1 is struck.
payoff: Function notation with expressions as inputs
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Replace every x with the whole input.

title: A rate goes from 10% to 15%. That's not a 5% increase
hook: A rate rises from 10% to 15%. By what percent did it increase?
insight: It rose 5 percentage points, but relative to where it started that is 5/10, a 50% increase. Percentage points measure the gap; percent change measures the gap against the start.
visual: Two bars at 10 and 15 stand on a percent axis; the 5-point gap is lifted off and laid on the original 10-bar, covering exactly half of it as 50% lights up.
payoff: percent change from a table of rates
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Know points versus percent before you see a table.

title: What is 0.5% of 200? It's not 100
hook: What is 0.5% of 200?
insight: 0.5% is half of one percent, not one half. 1% of 200 is 2, so 0.5% of 200 is 1.
visual: 200 squares fill a 10-by-20 grid, 1% lights up as 2 squares, then halves to a single blue square while the struck answer 100 fades.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Read the decimal in a percent before you multiply.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: A 5 cm metal cube weighs 1,000 g. Its density is not 200
hook: A metal cube with 5 cm edges has mass 1,000 grams. What's its density?
insight: Density is mass per volume, and the volume is 5^3 = 125 cubic centimeters, not 5. So the density is 1,000 / 125 = 8 grams per cubic centimeter.
visual: The cube fills with 125 small unit cubes layer by layer, the 1,000 g splits evenly among them, and each little cube reads 8 g.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Density isn't on the reference sheet. Know it cold.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: Boys to girls is 3:5. What fraction are girls? Not 3/5
hook: The ratio of boys to girls is 3 to 5. What fraction are girls?
insight: A part-to-part ratio splits the class into 3 + 5 = 8 equal shares, so girls are 5/8 of the class. 3/5 compares boys to girls, not girls to everyone.
visual: Eight tiles appear, three in ink and five in blue, and a bracket over all eight turns the 3:5 label into the fraction 5/8.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. This ratio trap shows up again and again.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: A 2-mile taxi ride costs $8. Does 4 miles cost $16?
hook: $2 plus $3 a mile: 2 miles cost $8. Do 4 miles cost $16?
insight: No, $14: only the $3-per-mile part doubles, the $2 fee doesn't. Doubling works only for proportional relationships, whose graphs pass through (0, 0).
visual: Points (1, 5), (2, 8), (4, 14) line up, the line extends back and hits the y-axis at 2 instead of the origin, while a dashed proportional line through the origin peels away toward the struck 16.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Doubling only works when the line hits the origin.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: 6 painters take 10 days. How long for 4 painters? Not 6.7
hook: Six painters finish a house in 10 days. How long would four take?
insight: The job is 6 x 10 = 60 painter-days of work. Fewer painters means more days: 60 / 4 = 15 days.
visual: A 6-by-10 grid of 60 painter-day cells reshapes into a 4-by-15 grid with the same blue area, while the struck guess 6.7 fades.
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Keep the total work fixed and this solves itself.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: Why cross-multiplying works, in one move
hook: Why can you cross-multiply a/b = c/d into ad = bc?
insight: Multiply both sides by b and by d. On the left the b cancels, on the right the d cancels, leaving ad = bc. The X is just a shortcut picture of that step.
visual: The equation a/b = c/d gets a bd multiplier on both sides, b and d cancel in place, and the two products slide along diagonal arcs into the familiar X.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Know why cross-multiplying works so you never misuse it.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
title: Pipes fill a tank in 3 and 6 hours. Together? Not 4.5
hook: One pipe fills a tank in 3 hours, another in 6. Together?
insight: Add rates, not times: 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 tank per hour, so together they take 2 hours. Two pipes must beat the faster pipe alone.
visual: A tank fills in two shades, the fast pipe pouring a third per hour and the slow pipe a sixth, and the shared water line reaches full at the 2-hour tick.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. Add rates, not times. Here's the picture.

title: What does 0.6 mean in w = 0.6d + 2? Say 'predicted'
hook: A pumpkin's best-fit weight is w = 0.6d + 2. What does 0.6 mean?
insight: The slope is the predicted increase in weight for each additional day, about 0.6 pounds. It describes the line, so no pumpkin is guaranteed to gain exactly 0.6 pounds a day.
visual: A slope triangle walks along the best-fit line one day at a time, each step rising 0.6, while the actual pumpkins' dots scatter above and below the steps.
payoff: interpreting the slope of a best-fit line
urgent_hook: {days} days until {test}. Interpreting slope is free points if you say 'predicted'.

title: Actual 34, predicted 30. Is the residual 4 or -4?
hook: A data point is at 34. The line predicts 30. What's the residual?
insight: Residual is actual minus predicted: 34 - 30 = 4. Points above the line have positive residuals, and points below have negative ones.
visual: A vertical stick drops from the dot at 34 to the line at 30, labeled +4 in blue, then a dot below the line gets an upward stick labeled negative.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Residual sign errors are free points lost. Fix it.

title: Why do you multiply probabilities for 'and'?
hook: Heads and a 6: why is the chance 1/2 times 1/6?
insight: Draw every outcome as a unit square: heads takes half the width, rolling a 6 takes a sixth of the height. Both happening is the corner rectangle, with area 1/2 x 1/6 = 1/12.
visual: A unit square splits vertically in half for the coin and horizontally into sixths for the die, and the single overlapping cell turns blue as 1/12.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. 'And' means multiply. Here's the picture that proves it.

skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
title: 62% plus or minus 4%: what does a margin of error mean?
hook: A survey finds 62% walk to school, margin of error 4%. What's true?
insight: It is plausible that between 58% and 66% of all students in the population walk to school. The margin is about the population percentage, not about individual students or a guarantee.
visual: A dot at 62% grows a blue bracket from 58 to 66 on a percent line, the label population attaches to the bracket, and choices about individual students strike through.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Margin of error questions have one right reading.

skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
title: A random sample of gym members. Who can you generalize to?
hook: 500 gym members, randomly sampled: exercisers sleep more. What can you conclude?
insight: Random sampling lets you generalize only to the population sampled, gym members, not all adults. And with no random assignment it shows an association, not that exercise causes better sleep.
visual: A circle of all gym members gives up a random scoop of 500 dots; an arrow back to the gym circle stays ink while arrows to all adults and to causes are struck.
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Know exactly who a sample speaks for.

skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
title: Why a coin flip is what lets a study claim cause
hook: Why does flipping a coin to assign groups let scientists say 'causes'?
insight: Random assignment spreads every hidden difference, like age, health and motivation, evenly across both groups on average. So if the groups end up different, the treatment is the only systematic difference left.
visual: A crowd with hidden traits shaded in different grays is split by coin flips, both groups show the same mix of shades, and then one group turns blue for the treatment.
urgent_hook: {days} days to {test}. One idea separates experiments from observational studies.

title: Slant height is not height
hook: A square pyramid has base edge 10 and slant height 13. Volume?
insight: The height is a leg of a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and other leg 5, half the base, so it is 12. Volume = 1/3 x 100 x 12 = 400, not 1/3 x 100 x 13.
visual: The pyramid is sliced through its tip, revealing a 5-12-13 right triangle standing inside it, and the vertical leg turns blue.
payoff: Pyramid and cone height from slant height
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Slant height hides a right triangle. Find it.

title: Perimeters 12 and 18. The area is not 30
hook: Similar triangles have perimeters 12 and 18. The smaller has area 20. Larger?
insight: Perimeter is a length, so the scale factor is 18 / 12 = 1.5. Area scales by 1.5^2 = 2.25, so the larger area is 45, not 30.
visual: The small triangle stretches into the large one while one readout multiplies the perimeter by 1.5 and the other multiplies the area by 2.25.
payoff: Similar figures: perimeter versus area ratio
urgent_hook: {test} is {days} days away. Perimeter scales by k, area by k squared.

title: Cutting a box in half adds surface area
hook: Cut a 2 by 3 by 4 box across its long side. Surface added?
insight: The cut creates two new 2 by 3 faces, so the surface area grows by 12, from 52 to 64. The volume stays 24.
visual: A blue plane slices the box, the two halves slide apart, and the two new 2 by 3 faces light up as the surface chip ticks from 52 to 64.
payoff: Surface area of cut or combined solids
urgent_hook: Retaking on {date}? Hard surface-area questions hide new faces. Count them.
